title: 1954 AHSME Problem 47
statement: At the midpoint of line segment \(\overline{AB}\) which is \(p\) units long, a perpendicular \(\overline{MR}\) is erected with length \(q\) units. An arc is described from \(R\) with a radius equal to \(\dfrac12\overline{AB},\) meeting \(\overline{AB}\) at \(T.\) Then \(\overline{AT}\) and \(\overline{TB}\) are the roots of:

solutions.text:
Let \(MT=t.\) Since \(AM=BM=RT=\frac{p}{2},\) the Pythagorean theorem gives \[ t^2+q^2=\frac{p^2}{4}. \] Also, \[ AT=\frac p2+t,\qquad TB=\frac p2-t. \] Their sum is \(p,\) and their product is \[ \frac{p^2}{4}-t^2=q^2. \] Therefore they are the roots of \(x^2-px+q^2=0.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Use \(RT=\frac{p}{2}=AM\) in right triangle \(RMT\) to show \(\overline{AT}\cdot\overline{TB}=q^2\)
